subject: Hosted API evaluation next steps and rate limits
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@finwise.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API evaluation next steps and rate limits

Hi Emily - great to meet today and thanks for taking the demo. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Recap of ask: FinWise wants a hosted evaluation of the Redwood Hosted API focused on chat summarization for customer support tickets (avg. 350 tokens in, 150 tokens out) and a goal of ~200 QPS across peak windows.

2) Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: As discussed, Hosted API is the fastest path to try functionality and measure latency/cost. Dedicated would be next if FinWise needs pinned capacity and isolated GPUs; Private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict data residency / compliance. For the eval please start with Hosted API - we can move to Dedicated for predictable sustained throughput later.

3) Proposed quickstart plan (attached):
   - Day 0: Provide sandbox API key + sample collection endpoints
   - Day 1-3: Run integration tests and one sample workload (100 QPS)
   - Day 4-7: Ramp to target QPS and share cost/latency breakdown

4) Rate limits & endpoints: Hosted API default rate limit for new eval accounts is 300 RPS aggregate (burstable) with token-based limits; per-key concurrency is enforced to avoid noisy neighbors. If you need sustained 200 QPS for inference, we recommend requesting a temporary uplift for the eval - we can provision a "burst capacity" increase for the week.

5) Next steps: 
   - I will create a sandbox project and share API keys and the quickstart artifacts (attached).
   - Please confirm who from FinWise will run the integration (email + Slack handle).
   - If procurement wants terms ahead of time I can loop in our contracts team and send the SLA summary.

Attachments: eval-plan.pdf, SLA-summary.pdf, redwood-quickstart.zip

Thanks - happy to hop on another 30m with your infra/ops person while they run the tests.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks for the clear recap, Aditya - this looks good. A few quick questions from our side before we start the sandbox: 

1) Can you confirm the exact throttling behavior? If we hit the per-key concurrency cap, will calls queue or return 429s? Do you support client-side exponential backoff recommended settings?

2) For data handling: during the hosted eval, will customer content be stored by Redwood? We need to confirm retention and whether we can enable opt-out for any data persistence.

3) For the uplift: who should I put on the request to get the temporary quota increased? We want to ramp to 200 QPS for a 3-day window.

People running the integration: me (emily.chen@finwise.com) and our infra engineer, David K. (david.k@finwise.com). Procurement is looped at procurement@finwise.com and may ask for the SLA doc.

If that all checks out we can start next Monday (June 14).

- Emily

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@finwise.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation next steps and rate limits

Emily - great questions. Short answers below, Neha has included more technical detail in a follow-up.

1) Throttling: For Hosted eval accounts we enforce per-key concurrency and aggregate RPS. If you exceed per-key concurrency calls will receive 429s; we do not queue long-running requests on the public hosted tier. We recommend client-side retry with exponential backoff (retry-after header returned when applicable).

2) Data handling: By default, Hosted API stores request metadata and short-term logs for 30 days for debugging. We can enable a data-retention opt-out for the eval (no long-term storage) and exclude logs from analytics on request if you need, I'll add the retention flag to your sandbox. For production, we can discuss Private/ Dedicated options if retention policies require that.

3) Uplift request: Please CC me on the request to support@redwood.ai and include the target QPS and window. I will fast-track it with our infra team. For this eval I will request a temporary uplift to 400 RPS to give headroom around the 200 QPS target.

I'll schedule the sandbox and share keys by end of day. If you want a quick sync with David and your infra engineer next week I can loop Marissa (solutions architect) to join.

Best,
Aditya
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@finwise.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation next steps and rate limits - technical details

Hi Emily - Neha from Solutions Engineering here. Adding a few tech specifics and a checklist to make the sandbox run smoothly: 

- Endpoints: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (chat) and POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings for embeddings. Use Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>. Sample curl in the quickstart (docs link attached).

- Rate limits: The sandbox will have an uplifted aggregate RPS of 400 for the week. Per-key concurrency default is 10 concurrent requests; if you need higher concurrency we can create multiple API keys or request a higher concurrency limit. Typical recommended client pattern is: 3 retries with exponential backoff starting at 200ms, and jitter. Watch for 429 and 503 responses and respect Retry-After.

- Payload guidance: For summarization we recommend batching up to 8 tickets per request (when possible) to improve throughput - the runtime supports efficient batching on the hosted tier. Keep prompt and system tokens within 4096 token total for the evaluation models we provisioned.

- Data retention: For this eval we will enable the "no-persist" flag so request content is not stored beyond ephemeral logs used for debugging (30-day auto-delete) and will not be used for training. We will provide a DPA snippet for procurement if needed.

- Quick checklist for Monday: 
  1) Confirm David K. Slack handle or email for a 30m warm-up call.
  2) Send uplift request to support@redwood.ai (cc aditya@redwood.ai).
  3) Confirm test suite you plan to run (1000 sample tickets or live shadow traffic).

I've attached a small test harness and a sample curl script in redwood-quickstart.zip. Ping me if you want us to run the ramp together.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai
